clue.text: Capital investment that makes speculators brood

definitions.note: something put on the head (the 'capital'), a guardsman's tall fur hat

parts.note: bears are stock-market speculators who bet on prices falling
a brood is one's offspring or family, one's kin

explanation.surface: A financial deal that makes stock-market dealers sulk or worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is the head, not money, and 'investment' is clothing (one is invested in it); 'brood' looks like a verb meaning sulk but is the noun for offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall black fur cap of British guardsmen is a headpiece, playfully called an investment for the head.

clue.text: Making a note to promote cook

parts.note: B is a musical note
to promote someone is to raise them in rank

explanation.surface: Writing a memo recommending the chef for promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Braising is a way of cooking food slowly in a little liquid in a closed pot.

clue.text: Hope for a father without money

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the father word goes round the money

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father
P stands for penny or pence, a small sum of money

explanation.surface: A wish for a dad who is broke.
explanation.definitionFit: To hope for something keenly is to set one's ambitions on it.

clue.text: Rogue putting a point about a politician

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
C is short for circa, Latin for about
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A scoundrel making a remark concerning a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rascal, a lovable villain.

clue.text: Search 22 with soft heart

indicators.note: placed at the heart of the earlier answer, so the soft letter goes into its middle

parts.note: the answer to 22 down, a six-footer, is a bug
p (piano) means soft in music

explanation.surface: Look for something, gently and kindly.
explanation.walkthrough: The 22 refers to the answer of 22 down; P goes into its middle, between INS and ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something is to examine it carefully, to look it over closely.

clue.text: A drug taken in Utopia-terribly soporific

indicators.note: the letters are taken in by the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A narcotic consumed in an ideal world proves terribly sleep-inducing.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles the hyphen: utOPIA-TErribly. 'soporific' just describes the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium-derived narcotics such as morphine are classed under this name.

clue.text: Pain people maybe, losing nothing but fruit

indicators.note: maybe suggests the words could be arranged differently, an anagram signal

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone annoys others, finally giving up nothing but a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' tells you the letters of PAIN PEOPLE, rearranged by 'maybe', must give up an O ('nothing'); the remaining nine form the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical plant bearing a large spiky-skinned juicy yellow fruit.

clue.text: The old will swallow it at getting all wound up

indicators.note: the elderly word swallows the next words, taking them inside itself

parts.note: the aged are old people
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Elderly people gulp it down at a time of great excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wound up means tense and nervous, flustered and upset.

clue.text: Nonetheless the head makes a constant appearance

parts.note: even so means nonetheless, shortened here to even
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Even so, the headteacher keeps turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniformity or steadiness gives something a constant look, level and regular throughout.

clue.text: Pop back to extol value

indicators.note: back means the word for pop is read backwards

parts.note: pop and pa are both words for father
to extol is to praise highly

explanation.surface: Dad returning to speak highly of something's worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess the worth of something, like an estate agent pricing a house.

clue.text: Pure in its ingredients, yet not fit to eat

indicators.note: the ingredients are mixed together, so the letters of pure in are mixed up

explanation.surface: Something wholesome in its contents, but still inedible.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is green and hard is not ready to be eaten.

clue.text: Part of a church that's in danger of collapse

indicators.note: the answer is a part that sits in the next word

explanation.surface: A section of a church building that is close to falling down.
explanation.walkthrough: collAPSE contains the answer; 'danger of' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: The semicircular recess at the east end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: The militant man's pile?

parts.note: a militant person loves a scrap or fight, so his heap would be a fighter's pile, a pun on the place where junk is thrown

explanation.definitionFit: A rubbish tip of discarded junk metal, here reimagined as a heap for one who likes fights.

clue.text: Making a return once more

parts.note: a return on an investment is a gain or profit

explanation.surface: Making a profit for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something once more is repeating it one further time.

clue.text: Rapidly dissipated

definitions.meaning: as in rushing or flying by, going swiftly beyond
gone, over and done with, as in 'the danger is over'

explanation.definitionFit: Speeding by something is going beyond it; a passion that has dissipated is over and done with.

clue.text: The speed really doesn't matter however

definitions.meaning: read literally, whatever the pace is is acceptable
used as a phrase meaning anyway, in any case

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, whichever pace; as an idiom it means anyway or nevertheless, a connective like however.

clue.text: Lacking iron say

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Having no metal, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to put it into words, to state it.

clue.text: Carol set about 21 for twisting

indicators.note: the singing word is set round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
the answer to 21 across, the company of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone named Carol tackles the company for a contortion.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving in a screw involves turning it, so the participle means rotating or twisting.

clue.text: Continue favouring a certain area of the country

parts.note: pro means in favour of

parts.words: a certain area of the country
parts.note: a tract is a stretch of land

explanation.surface: Keep supporting a particular region.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract something is to prolong it, to keep it going longer.

clue.text: Short article on inside cover

parts.note: curt means short or brusque in manner
a is the indefinite article
in means inside

explanation.surface: A brief piece of writing about an inner covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape over a window or stage hides what lies behind it, screening it from view.

clue.text: An outstanding feature!

parts.note: outstanding is read literally as standing out from the face, a facial feature that protrudes

explanation.definitionFit: The organ of smell projects from the middle of the face.

clue.text: The company boasted superiority

definitions.meaning: a group working together, as on a ship or film set
crowed, an old past tense of crow, to gloat triumphantly

explanation.definitionFit: A team of sailors or workers is a company; the archaic past of crow, to gloat, is spelt the same.

clue.text: Get overcrowded and study gets affected

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: affected in the sense of changed or acted upon, so the letters of gets are altered

explanation.surface: Things become crowded and studying is disrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets that congest become blocked with too much traffic.

clue.text: A six-footer popular with the party

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a sect is a faction or party

explanation.surface: A very tall person well liked by the political group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it means a creature with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, so a creature with six feet is one of them.

clue.text: Holy man held by a member of the nobility to cause trouble

indicators.note: the holy man is held inside the noble word

parts.note: a peer is a member of the House of Lords, a noble
St is short for saint

explanation.surface: A saint detained by an aristocrat, creating a disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester someone is to bother or harass them persistently.

clue.text: Points to attempt to gain access

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass points
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Advice on trying to get in somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission into a place is the right or means of getting in.

clue.text: Awareness as a result of some words written about the unit

indicators.note: the words are written around the unit, enclosing it

parts.note: a sentence is a group of words
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: Consciousness arising from a few words penned on the subject of a single thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient beings can feel and perceive, so this means consciousness or feeling.

clue.text: Woman putting her all into Ernie

indicators.note: putting effort into something works it over, so the letters of the name are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman making every effort for Ernie.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so a woman.

clue.text: Ai band playing in a Nigerian place

indicators.note: a band playing makes music, and the letters play into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A top-class band performing in a Nigerian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The ai is a three-toed sloth, a crossword favourite, here just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in south-western Nigeria, capital of Oyo State.

clue.text: Forceful macho guys interrupting judge

indicators.note: the macho word interrupts the judge word, breaking into it

parts.note: to vet is to examine and judge
he-men are macho men

explanation.surface: Tough men butting in on a judge forcefully.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement argument is passionate and intense.

clue.text: The weapon of a woman, so one might assume

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman's weapon, one might suppose.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather is to infer or conclude, as in 'I gather you're leaving'.

clue.text: When a totter's upset he swears!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: A wobbly person falls over and curses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns TOTTERS into TTESTOR, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: One who attests formally declares something true, as a witness under oath.
